cards.text: The LORD is still speaking through His prophet Jeremiah, warning His people that judgment is coming on Jerusalem. And this part opens like a smoke alarm going off at 3 a.m. “Run for cover, O sons of Benjamin; flee from Jerusalem!”

cards.question: The LORD says to sound the ram’s horn in Tekoa and send up a signal over Beth-haccherem. What’s coming?

cards.text: Then the LORD calls the Daughter of Zion beautiful and delicate. Friend, nobody has EVER called me delicate, and I’m a cookie stamper with a mustache.

cards.question: True or false: Because the Daughter of Zion is beautiful and delicate, the LORD will spare her.

cards.text: Shepherds and their flocks will come against her. They’ll pitch their tents all around her, each one tending his own portion, like folks setting out lawn chairs on the curb the night before a parade.
Then we hear the attackers plotting: “Prepare for battle against her; rise up, let us attack at noon.” But then they cry, “Woe to us, for the daylight is fading…”

cards.question: The attackers wanted to strike at noon, but now the evening shadows are growing long. What’s their new plan?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts speaks: “Cut down the trees and raise a siege ramp against Jerusalem.” That’s not a quick visit, friend, that’s somebody planning to STAY.

cards.question: The LORD orders a siege ramp against Jerusalem and says this city must be ___. There is nothing but oppression in her midst.

cards.text: The LORD puts it like this: “As a well gushes its water, so she pours out her evil.” Friend, picture a fire hydrant somebody cracked open in July.

cards.question: Violence and destruction resound in Jerusalem. True or false: The LORD says her sickness and wounds are ever before Him.
Even now, the LORD tells Jerusalem to be forewarned. If she isn’t, what does He say He’ll do?

answers.text: Turn away and make her a desolation
Send her a new king from Egypt
Scatter her people across the sea

cards.text: Next the LORD of Hosts reaches for a picture from the vineyard: “Glean the remnant of Israel as thoroughly as a vine.”

cards.question: True or false: In this vineyard picture, the LORD says to pass a hand over the branches once more, like a grape gatherer.

cards.text: Then we hear, “To whom can I give this warning? Who will listen to me?” Somebody just got left on read by a WHOLE CITY.

cards.question: The people’s ears are closed, so they can’t hear. The word of the LORD has become ___ to them.

cards.text: Then the next line says, “But I am full of the LORD’s wrath; I am tired of holding it back.” And then come the words, “Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the young men gathered together.”

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says husbands and wives will be captured, but the old and the very old will be spared.
The LORD says He will stretch out His hand against the people of the land. What happens to their houses?

cards.text: Then the LORD says why: from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain. Mailroom to corner office, friend, EVERYBODY.

cards.question: Even the prophets and the priests are in on it. What does the LORD say they all practice?

cards.text: The LORD says they dress the wound of His people with very little care. That’s one tiny cartoon bandage on a broken arm and calling it a day.

cards.question: The wound of the LORD’s people gets very little care. What do the ones dressing it say?
The LORD asks if they’re ashamed of the abomination they’ve committed. His answer: no, they have no shame at all. They don’t even know how to ___.

cards.text: So the LORD says they will fall among the fallen, and when He punishes them, they will collapse. That’s a heavy word, friend, so let it sit for a minute.
